spec_match.rationale: Demonstrates the design rationale the spec PR argues: the getter-based detectability of a dictionary member versus the undetectable third positional argument, using the exact WebSocketInit surface.

interactive.rationale: Run both probes executes two real constructions and updates both verdict panels and the aria-live detail; on Chromium 141 it honestly reported the getter never fired and the positional argument left nothing observable.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The card frames this as the argument for the shape with feature detection both ways, which is what the page does.

edge_cases.rationale: Both verdict branches handle construction throwing, and the definite-no outcome on an old browser is presented as equally useful rather than as an error.

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5080055102439424 and the WebSocketInit spec PR.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite's getter-read assertion is exactly this page's dictionary probe; /conformance/ ran 5 pass / 1 fail on Chromium 141 with only that Chrome-154 assertion failing.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): clicked Run both probes, verdicts updated to the honest pre-154 outcomes (getter never fired; construction threw SyntaxError for '[object Object]'), console had only intentional logs, no failed same-origin requests; desktop and mobile screenshots read.

telemetry_health.rationale: Loads demo-telemetry.js and emits a detection-compared assert with both probe outcomes.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, good/bad panel colours from accent variables, button colour pair overridden together, live probes rather than a static card.

accessibility.rationale: Sections are aria-labelledby their headings, code samples are tabindex-0 focusable, the comparison table has caption and scoped th cells, and the outcome is an aria-live output.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: No horizontal page overflow at 360x740 DPR3 (scrollWidth 360, screenshot read); code panels scroll internally via overflow-x:auto.

summary: Reviewed at http://localhost:3000/v154/add-options-bag-to-websocket-constructor/why-a-dictionary/ with Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp). Clicked Run both probes via CDP: the dictionary probe reported a definite no (getter never fired, construction threw the '[object Object]' SyntaxError) and the positional probe reported nothing observable — precisely the honest pre-Chrome-154 outcome the page is designed to teach, so the demo's core lesson works even without the feature. Desktop 1280 and mobile 360 DPR3 screenshots read with no overflow; console/network clean bar the sandbox font-CDN cert artifact; injected browser-support panel and /conformance/ both ran 5 pass / 1 fail with only the dictionary-read assertion needing Chrome 154. Clears the bar with no follow-ups.
